MG01.analysis: Socks: soft, can pad. Ruler: thin, brittle, but can wedge into a seam if gap opens. Hat: useless. Hairbrush: useless. Rubber band: stretched, weak grip. Wooden spoon handle: hard, smooth, usable as mallet. Useful: wooden spoon, ruler, socks. Tapping around the lid breaks the seal and loosens it; then a wedge lifts it.
MG01.final:
Step1: Wrap the spoon bowl in a sock and tap firmly around the lid edge and corners to break the seal.
Step2: Once a hairline gap shows, slide the ruler in and run it around the seam to break the vacuum, then lift the lid.
VERDICT: SOLVABLE

MG02.analysis: Bucket: carry water/soil. Paintbrush: clear loose soil. Comb: comb out roots. Hose: high-pressure water erodes rocky soil (air-spade-like). Soup spoon: scoop slurry. Gloves: weak, marginal. Useful: hose, bucket, spoon, brush. Water jetting replaces digging.
MG02.final:
Step1: Use the high-pressure hose to jet and loosen soil around the planting spot, forming a hole.
Step2: Scoop out the slurry with the bucket and spoon; repeat until deep and wide enough.
Step3: Set the trees, backfill with the muddy slurry, and water in.
VERDICT: SOLVABLE

MG03.analysis: Beam: curved, but can serve as a ridge/support if wedged. Tarp: holey, but can be folded double/triple so holes do not align. Pitchfork: can prop the beam or hold tarp edges. Screws: fasten tarp to coop walls/beam. Lawn chair: stand on to reach. Rope: weak, only light tying. Useful: beam, tarp, screws, chair, pitchfork.
MG03.final:
Step1: Stand on the lawn chair, lay the curved beam across the coop top with the curve upward as a ridge, and prop it with the pitchfork if needed.
Step2: Fold the tarp into 2-3 layers so holes are offset, drape it over the beam.
Step3: Screw the tarp edges to the coop walls; tie slack with the rope.
VERDICT: SOLVABLE

MG04.analysis: Curler and hairdryer: useless. Vinegar: allergy, rule out. Olive oil: suffocates and lubricates lice; little is enough if used sparingly. Shower cap: holds oil in, fragile but fine for one session. Fine-tooth comb: removes lice and nits. Useful: olive oil, shower cap, fine comb.
MG04.final:
Step1: Work the small amount of olive oil through the damp hair, concentrating on the scalp and nape.
Step2: Cover with the shower cap for several hours or overnight to smother lice.
Step3: Comb section by section with the fine-tooth comb, wiping it each pass; repeat every 2-3 days for two weeks.
VERDICT: SOLVABLE

MG05.analysis: Index cards: insulating spacer. Aluminum foil: conductive shim. Vinegar: dissolves corrosion on contacts. Thread: useless. Cotton swabs: apply vinegar. Spare button battery: wrong size but may supply the right voltage (1.5V) and be shimmed. Useful: vinegar, swabs, foil, card, button battery.
MG05.final:
Step1: Dab vinegar on the corroded contacts with cotton swabs and wipe dry.
Step2: Fold foil into a pad to fill the gap so the smaller button battery touches both terminals with correct polarity; insulate any stray contact with an index card scrap.
Step3: Check the clock runs (battery voltage must match).
VERDICT: SOLVABLE

MG06.analysis: Bat: sturdy-ish handle extender, worn. Rope: lash things together. Soda can: useless/weight. Tarp: protect ground from drips. Tires: deflated, poor platform. Bamboo: thin, cannot hold body weight but can be lashed into a long pole for the brush. Useful: bamboo, rope, tarp. Paint from the ground using extension.
MG06.final:
Step1: Lay the tarp at the wall base to catch drips.
Step2: Lash several bamboo lengths end to end with overlapping joints and the rope (bat as optional brace) to form a long pole.
Step3: Tie the brush to the tip and paint the high section from the ground, working in sections.
VERDICT: SOLVABLE

MG07.analysis: Protractor: measure incline angle. Ruler as ramp, sandpaper as surface (or test surface). Weights: act as the sliding block. Pencil/nail: pivot and marker. Rubber band, stopwatch, goggles: not needed. Inclined plane method: mu = tan(theta) at the angle where sliding starts, no force sensor needed.
MG07.final:
Step1: Place a weight on a flat board/ruler surface covered with the test material (e.g. sandpaper).
Step2: Slowly tilt it, propping with pencil/nail, until the weight just begins to slide; read the angle with the protractor.
Step3: Compute mu = tan(angle); repeat a few times and average.
VERDICT: SOLVABLE

MG08.analysis: Broom handle and plank: could pry, but plank is termite-weak and the steel door is heavy and jammed. Bucket: weak lever. Kite: cannot carry a person. Torch: signalling only. Rope: only 15 ft against a ten-story drop (~100+ ft). No safe descent route and no tool strong enough to open the door.
MG08.final:
Step1: Not possible to get to the ground yourself: 15 ft of rope covers about one floor of a ten-story building, the kite cannot lift a person, and none of the tools can force a jammed steel door.
Only signalling for rescue (torch, kite) is feasible, which does not satisfy self-descent.
VERDICT: UNSOLVABLE

MG09.analysis: Crossword book: could shade a bit, flimsy. Poncho: torn, usable as layer. Two sticks: supports. Snorkel and fins: fins can anchor/prop. Steel mug: fill with sand as weight. Large beach towel: main shade, intact. Useful: towel, sticks, poncho, mug, fins.
MG09.final:
Step1: Drive the two sticks upright into the sand, a few feet apart, bracing with sand piled in the mug and fins.
Step2: Drape the beach towel over the sticks, with the poncho layered over it to cover gaps; weigh the edges with sand or the mug.
VERDICT: SOLVABLE

MG10.analysis: Rope 10 ft: too short. Stool: heavy, gives only a little height. Cloth: useless. Bottle: throwable. Rock: throwable, hits bell and rings it; ringing needs contact, not hand reach. Optionally tie rock to rope to retrieve. Useful: rock, rope, bottle.
MG10.final:
Step1: Stand on the stool for extra height and throw the rock (or the bottle) at the bell so it strikes and rings it.
Step2: Retry as needed; optionally tie the rope to the rock to retrieve it.
VERDICT: SOLVABLE
